author: reek
body: A `let` bound inside an `if` arm does not escape the arm, so a later read of that name finds whatever was in scope all along -- here, a GLOBAL of a different type.

author: reek
body: This is the direction that makes the leak visible as a REJECTION rather than a miscompile. `env-bind-local` reached the caller's environment through `__record-set`, which is an in-place field store returning the same record, so the arm's `inner : Integer` stayed bound after the arm ended and shadowed the global `inner : Text` at the read. The checker then rejected this file with CDX2001 (Text vs Integer) -- a valid program the emitter would have compiled correctly, refused by the type checker alone.

author: reek
body: `act-let-scope` pins the sibling rule (an act-block let DOES scope over the rest of the block) and `arm-local: 23` there pins the emitter's half of this one. This file pins the CHECKER's half: the two must agree about the same program, and until 2.22 they did not.
